shared-needs.rule: shared/ belongs to the shared author (brief C, "What R-03 produces"); this volume never writes it and never points into it before it exists. Each need names the volume and the anchor the shared author declares, using the anchor name of the node that owns the thing (envelope and cas from N-01, record-kinds-registry from N-18, codes from N-43, break-glass from N-27). check.sh (N-46) resolves a need by volume and anchor once the shared volume lands, so a need becomes a live pointer without a hand edit. The same needs are returned to the shared author as data by the seat that wrote this volume.
shared-needs.need: Rows for controls.rendered 200; control.recorded 201; control.conflict 409; controls.held 423; hold.ignored 500; controls.stale 503; controls.view-timeout 504. Owner-acts: hold.ignored (a tick ran a dispatch under a hold; one card).
A lamp column per code (green, amber or red) so a screen draws a code without a table of its own; N-37 generates bindings from it and the signal lamp, the watcher lamp and the health dots read it.
The record envelope every kind carries: id, at (UTC), code, kind, node, attempt where one applies; this node reads and writes records only inside it.
Compare-and-swap: expected_version on an entity write; 409 with the current version on a miss; expected 0 inserts.
The hold flag is an entity every tick reads before dispatch; set and cleared by compare-and-swap on its version; a tick that dispatches under a set flag writes 500 hold.ignored.
entities(key, version, body, updated_at): hold.flag, build-mode.state and break-glass.token are entities; two owner devices acting at once yield one 201 and one 409.
build_mode(state, scope, expires_at, ruling_id): the build-mode lever reads and writes this table through N-44, never a file.
idempotency(key PRIMARY KEY, seq, response JSON, at); a seen key replays its response with code 200.

The record kinds registry (every kind with its code set, writer node and schema path, loaded by N-43 with the code table) carries the kinds this node reads and writes: controls.frame (N-31), hold.flag, build-mode.state (N-44), watcher.alive (N-27), health (N-06), card (N-28), ruling (N-29), break-glass.token, control.action (origin page or break-glass).
owner_key and viewer_key (N-32), hold.effect_timeout_s (60), watcher.heartbeat_timeout_s (30).

The owner key in the first URL becomes the cookie and is the only credential that renders an action; the viewer key draws the panel read-only; no seat ever holds either key, writes a control.action, a ruling, a hold flag or a token; a seat that needs a ruling posts a card (N-28) and leaves.

Break glass is owner-only and one time: the token is minted by a ruling on a card (N-29), consumed by compare-and-swap, recorded as control.action with origin break-glass; when the page is unreachable the same record is posted through the Go service CLI on the host and read back before acting; N-51 counts every such record.
Every control.action is a new traversal at N-29: one ruling per action id, replay by the same id a 409 no-op.
A card cannot post unless a watcher.alive for that tier is fresh (the C32 defect fix); the watcher lamp on this screen is that record.
No cog: every wait has a timeout and a fallback, nothing starts by an agent typing, no agent is a gate; the system drives (brief C rule 3).
Many agents at once from the first line: append-only records, compare-and-swap, idempotent retryable steps, conflicts that report as 409 (brief C rule 2).
Every automated step retries up to 3 times with backoff, then recovers and reports as a record; a dead record becomes exactly one card.
The owner's always-on monitor never stops on a halt; a HOLD dims actions, never the screens (brief C, command center volume).
Push transport for everything; a client re-reads full state on reconnect and drops any frame older than the one it holds (D21).
Build mode is a flag with an expiry set by a ruling, never a mode a seat declares; this screen shows it and lets the owner set it, nothing else.

purpose.s: The reactor panel: the signal lamp HOLD or USERGO, the halt lever with its two-step confirm, the watcher lamp per tier, build mode with its expiry, the system's health, the owner's open decision cards, and the last owner action with its UTC time (wireframe-brief.json screen Controls; C32 approved). Primary action: pull the halt lever.

The owner is the only operator and the only break glass (no-cog); every action here is a record that enters the DAG at N-29 as a ruling, so a gate reads a record and never a chat line (memory rulings-gates-check-are-records).
The C32 defect fix lives here: a card cannot be posted unless a watcher for that tier is alive, and the Controls screen shows the watcher as a lamp (HANDOFF.md, defect found 2026-10-14 ~04:10Z).

input.s: N-31 pushes the controls frame: the hold flag (signal HOLD or USERGO with its ruling id and since; merge.hold from N-10 with the red main sha), the build-mode state (N-44: on or off, expiry, ruling id), the watcher.alive lamps per tier (N-27: tier, pid, last heartbeat, lock path), the health record (N-06: gRPC Health status, counters, tick age), the open cards (N-28: id, about, decide, options, recommendation, posted at), the last ruling (N-29: card or action id, pick, words, at), and the break-glass token state (minted, consumed, or none).

output.s: A control.action record, owner-initiated, with an action id the client mints (idempotency key), the action (hold, resume, build-mode-on with expiry, build-mode-off, break-glass with the target), the expected version of the flag it changes (compare-and-swap), the owner's words, and at UTC. It enters N-29 as an answer record and becomes a ruling; N-44 reads build-mode rulings, N-07 reads the hold flag, N-10 reads a break-glass ruling for a held merge.

Draws controls.frame on screen (not stored). A second action on the same flag version is refused 409 and shown; break glass is one time: the token is consumed by compare-and-swap and a second use is 409.

panels.panel: Title Controls, the operator line (the owner is the only operator; read-only while offline with the last known time), the health dot of the Go service.
CURRENT signal with its big lamp (HOLD red, USERGO green) and since; NEXT on request; merge.hold shown as an amber lamp with the red main sha; the Give USERGO or Hold button (owner key).
The lever in three positions (rest, armed, pulled) with the two-step confirm: 1 Arm the lever (disarms itself after 10 s), 2 Confirm halt; the result line.
One lamp per bearings tier (stable, uat, dev when up): green with the heartbeat age when a wait loop holds the lock, red with "no watcher, cards cannot post" otherwise.
Build mode on or off, the expiry countdown in UTC, the ruling that set it; the Turn on with expiry and Turn off buttons (owner key).
Go service health (serving or not), tick age, store seq, backups last at, push clients connected.
Open decision cards from the system lane with about, decide and the recommendation; Open Getting My Bearings; the count; the empty block when none.
When (UTC), action, result of the last ruling or control action; the empty block when none recorded.
The one-time break glass: token state, what it would bypass (a merge.hold or a dead record on one named ticket), the two-step confirm; consumed tokens listed with their time.

mechanism.diagram: flowchart LR F[N-31 controls frame: hold, build-mode, watcher, health, cards, last ruling, token] --> C[client: controls module] C --> D[controls.frame drawn] C -->|owner key: hold, resume, build-mode, break glass| A[control.action: action id, expected version] A --> R[N-29 owner answer intake: ruling record] R --> H[N-07 reads hold flag] R --> B[N-44 build-mode flag with expiry] R --> G[N-10 reads break-glass ruling for a held merge] R -->|409 version changed or token consumed| C W[N-27 watcher.alive] --> F K[N-28 cards: refused without watcher.alive] --> F

step.s: The frame is drawn from the push; the action buttons are enabled only on the owner key and only while the stream is live (offline is read-only: "Halt needs a live connection. Reconnect first, or use the owner break-glass path." from the approved frame).

Every action is a control.action with a client-minted action id (UUID) as idempotency key and the expected version of the flag it changes, taken from the frame; the server applies compare-and-swap at N-01 and N-29 records the ruling; 201 with the new version, or 409 with the current state.

N-29 treats a control.action as an answer record whose card id is the action id; one ruling per action id; a second answer to the same action id is refused (dag.md section 4 re-entry rule). The hold flag is the entity flag:hold with a version (shared/state-store.xml#flag-hold), drawn through the hold.flag view (nodes/N-31/spec.xml#views); N-07 reads it level-triggered every tick, so a hold takes effect within one tick and nothing is typed to any seat.

Halt stops every agent except monitoring: N-07 dispatches nothing while hold is set; N-12 keeps its stall timers; N-15 running seats finish their one shot or are stopped by the halt ruling's stop-running flag (owner's choice on the confirm step); the bearings stable page, its wait loops, the push transport and the map keep running (bearings-stable-is-the-only-always-on-monitor; R-08 note: a halt never stops the owner monitoring surface).

Watcher lamp and the card rule: N-27 holds a lock with a heartbeat per tier; N-28 refuses to post a card with a clear 423 record unless watcher.alive for that tier is fresh; the lamp shows the same record; a red lamp on stable while cards are pending is an alert (N-41) and the one thing the system cannot fix by itself: N-28 holds the card three times with backoff and then writes card.unwatched 500, which is an alert row here and, once live, a phone push (N-52); a card is never moved to another tier, because a uat or dev deck is not the owner's deck (the one rule: nodes/N-28/spec.xml#mechanism step 5).

actions.action: Arm (10 s self-disarm), then Confirm halt with the stop-running choice (finish one-shots, or stop them now); result: hold.flag signal HOLD, N-07 dispatches nothing, monitoring keeps running.

Give USERGO (shared/cut-over.xml#signals: USERGO clears flag:hold; GOFACTORY does not and is given on its own card, N-30 R03); the confirm line names how many machines are stalled ("4 machines are stalled; the line starts anyway if you say so"); result: flag:hold cleared by compare-and-swap with the ruling id, signal USERGO; a USERGO before GOFACTORY is refused with a reply naming the hold (N-30 R02); the GOFACTORY ruling N-49 and N-50 read is a separate card, never this button.
Turn on with an expiry the owner picks (1 h, 6 h, 24 h, 7 d) or turn off; result: a ruling N-44 applies; the flag clears itself at expiry (N-44), never by a seat.

One time, owner only: pick the one target (a merge.hold on a named sha, or a dead record on a named ticket) and confirm; the token is minted by a prior ruling on a card (N-29) and consumed by compare-and-swap; result: a ruling N-10 or N-03 reads once; the token is gone; a second use is 409; the action and its target are an alert row so it is never silent.
actions.s: No other action exists on the page: no per-ticket retry, kill or merge (D15: the owner holds the line through cards, never the per-PR path).

states.state: Signal HOLD with USERGO next, lever at rest with the three positions drawn, watcher lamps per tier, build mode off, health serving, one open card, the last action with its UTC time.

No cards and no action ever recorded: the empty blocks ("No open decision cards" with Open Getting My Bearings as the real button; "None recorded yet" for the last action); the lever and signal still drawn.
Skeleton blocks in the shape of the panel; no centred spinner.
not-found (the controls view is absent), timeout (no frame within 10 s), validation (frame failed schema); what to do next and Retry.

Read-only with the last known frame and time; every action button disabled with the reason; the break-glass path line names the owner-only recovery (runbook); no queued action on this screen because an action must act on a live version.

start.s: The controls frame is pushed as soon as the Go service serves; the client subscribes on open; the owner acts when he chooses; nothing is typed to any seat. Ships in the N-38 bundle, promoted by N-48.

wait.name: controls-first-frame
wait.fallback: error state class timeout with Retry; automatic retry continues
wait.s: From the subscription to the first controls frame.

wait.name: controls-staleness
wait.fallback: stale chip (503) and every action disabled; at 60 s offline banner
wait.s: Actions need a live version; a stale frame disables them rather than risk a 409 storm.

wait.name: arm-self-disarm
wait.fallback: the lever returns to rest; nothing recorded
wait.s: The two-step confirm's first step expires on its own.

wait.name: action-reply
wait.fallback: resend with the same action id and expected version up to 3 times; then the result line says not recorded and the button re-enables; never a silent drop and never a second action id

wait.name: hold-takes-effect
wait.fallback: if N-07 dispatches after a hold ruling (a dispatch record newer than the ruling), that is a 500 hold.ignored alert and one card; the hold ruling itself stands
wait.s: One tick; the page shows the signal change the moment the ruling lands and the dispatch count stop on the next tick.

wait.name: watcher-heartbeat
wait.fallback: lamp red; N-28 refuses cards for that tier with 423; alert row; one card on another watched tier or the phone bridge

retries.s: Client sends retry 3 times with the same action id and version, then recover into a visible not-recorded line; the owner may act again, which mints a new action id against the current version. Server-side, a ruling is one record; there is nothing to retry; a flag a node ignores is an alert and a card.

many-agents.s: Readers: every client draws the same controls frame; only owner-key clients can act; N viewer clients cost N subscriptions.

Two owner devices acting at once (the phone and the desktop): both send against the same flag version; compare-and-swap lets one win 201 and answers the other 409 with the new state; both screens end identical; no double hold, no double resume, no lost action.

An action racing a system change: merge.hold set by N-10 bumps the hold.flag version; an owner resume sent against the old version gets 409 and the screen shows the red main first, so the owner resumes knowing main is red (or uses break glass once, deliberately).

Break glass under concurrency: the token is one record; consumption is compare-and-swap from minted to consumed with the action id; two uses at once yield one 201 and one 409; a replay of the same action id is a 409 no-op.

Many seats under a hold: the hold is a flag every tick reads (J18: halt as a flag every loop reads), not a message to each seat, so twenty running seats are stopped or allowed to finish by one record; no seat is told anything, and no seat can miss it.

Cards from many sources at once: N-28 builds cards idempotently by source id and refuses without watcher.alive; the open-cards panel lists them all by id; answering is on the bearings page (N-29), one answer per card id.

status-codes.code: Frame drawn and current; actions enabled on the owner key.
A control.action landed and became a ruling; new flag version returned.
Flag version changed, token consumed or action id replayed; current state shown; nobody acts.
An action was refused because the page is stale or offline, or a card was refused by N-28 because no watcher is alive for the tier.
A dispatch landed after a hold ruling; alert and one card.
No frame or heartbeat within 10 s; actions disabled.
No frame within 10 s; error state, retrying.

permissions.s: Build seat: writes tools/map/src/controls/**, the Controls #panels of this volume, and tests; the control.action intake at N-29 and the hold flag read at N-07 are G5 and G2 tickets (shared needs).

Actions require the owner key; the viewer key draws the panel read-only. No seat ever writes a control.action, a ruling, a hold flag or a token; a seat that needs a ruling posts a card (N-28) and leaves.
Break glass is owner-initiated and one time; nothing automates it; the token is minted only by a ruling on a card.

monitoring.s: The watcher lamp is the monitor of the monitor: it is the one record the owner reads to know a card can reach him. The health panel shows the Go service's own gRPC Health and tick age. A hold the system ignores is a 500 alert and one card. The map draws N-42 as a machine whose lamp is the latest controls code.

runbook.s: Owner break-glass path when the page is unreachable: a ruling record posted through the Go service's CLI on the host (reading the record back before acting), the clause shared/seat-contract.xml#break-glass declared in #shared-needs; it is one time and recorded like a page action.

Watcher down on stable: the tools/bearings wait loop is a supervised unit (N-27); restart is the unit's job; the lamp turns green when the lock heartbeat resumes; a card refused meanwhile is re-posted by N-28 on the next tick, never by hand.
Cleanup: nothing on disk from this screen; store tables by N-45 retention; the watcher lock by N-27.
